answers.answer: Each player takes twelve ordinary turns in the standard 16-round game. A courtship space has no ordinary player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use; it is a courtship event only.
answers.evidence: Overview: “each player takes twelve ordinary turns.” It says courtship has “no player turns, service rotation, monument income or Servants’ Hall use.”

answers.answer: Hosting order: rotate service (Quarters to Available, then Expended to Quarters); resolve the round-track event; resolve applicable monuments and Servants’ Hall in either order; choose an activity tile; invite exactly the required gentry; provide all required service; resolve all positive favours before negative favours; optionally buy; clean up by sending every used servant to Expended Service, played gentry to personal discard, and returning the tile to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading it as required. The last player advances the marker.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Hosting steps 1–8: “resolve the round event first,” then ongoing effects; cleanup sends servants to Expended Service, gentry to personal discard, and returns/flips the tile.

answers.answer: Passing order: all servants directly to Available Service; all gentry in personal discard to hand; round-track event then ongoing tile effects; choose £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; the last player advances the marker. A Butler’s Room hire is an activity, not a passing benefit. The summary gives no hiring as a pass benefit.
answers.evidence: Passing: “all servants directly to Available Service → all gentry in your discard to hand → round-track event, then ongoing tile effects → choose £200 or a free Market refresh → optional one tile purchase.” It states Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit.

answers.answer: Yes. The activity and its PR6 guests are screened using reputation at the end of step 2 (6.1); four subsequent Service Help actions may lower actual reputation without invalidating the activity. Each action costs 3 reputation increments and moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service. It cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Reputation screening is fixed “at the end of step 2” and remains the screening level even if special actions later lower actual reputation. Service Help: “Lose 3 increments; move one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service.”

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; the order within either group is otherwise chosen. At minimum reputation you cannot reorder a negative reputation favour to avoid it; losses beyond the minimum are ignored, but the negative favour remains mandatory. A guest with a money penalty requires that penalty to be fully payable, using positive money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money; if short, you must borrow if possible, and if unable to fund it you cannot play that guest.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6 requires “all positive favours before all negative favours.” The reputation/money section says you “cannot take a negative favour first to shelter it at minimum reputation” and details fully paying money penalties.

answers.answer: Borrow Money costs 2 reputation increments for £100 and is repeatable. Service Help costs 3 increments to move one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service and is repeatable. Refresh Market costs 4 increments and is limited to once per turn for this special action. At minimum reputation, a player cannot take a special action. Service Help cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Special actions table lists all costs and limits; the preceding rule says at minimum “you cannot…take a special action.” Service Help specifies Quarters to Available and excludes taking directly from Expended Service.

answers.answer: Host Butler’s Room as a Servant Hiring activity, using an available butler or underbutler and no gentry. Take up to two servants from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutlers, into Expended Service; there is no money fee. The used butler is expended and the room upgrades on first use. Its upgraded side instead lets you recruit one common servant (footman, valet, or lady’s maid) from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service, instead of hiring up to two from supply; unique servants cannot be recruited.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring, Butler’s Room: “no gentry,” up to two from supply into Expended Service; upgraded room recruits one common servant from any location on one opponent’s board.

answers.answer: A housekeeper substitutes for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. A footman substitutes for a valet only if Brushing Room is in your tableau and no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, or footman) even while that regular type remains available.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: housekeeper and footman substitution conditions are stated; underbutler “may substitute for any base male servant…even when that type remains available.”

answers.answer: The only way to acquire an underbutler is purchasing Butler’s Pantry; take one from supply immediately into Expended Service. Butler’s Room and Hire Servant VP cards cannot hire one. The summary does not specify a separate time restriction on purchasing Butler’s Pantry or availability timing beyond immediate placement in Expended Service. Another player cannot recruit it: the upgraded Butler’s Room recruits only a common servant, and unique servants cannot be recruited.
answers.evidence: “Butler’s Pantry: purchasing it is the only way to acquire an underbutler; take one from the supply immediately into Expended Service.” Butler’s Room recruit option is limited to common servants; unique servants cannot be recruited.

answers.answer: In the Market, pay the space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier. In the Reserve, the base price is £300 plus the modifier. The price cannot be below £100. You cannot buy a duplicate tile you already own, but reputation does not restrict buying a tile above your reputation.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: Market space price plus modifier; Reserve base £300 plus modifier; minimum £100; never acquire a duplicate; reputation does not restrict purchasing.

answers.answer: When a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into the rightmost spaces. A drawn duplicate stacks on its matching Market tile and you draw again; if filling multiple spaces, sort only the newly drawn tiles by ascending sorting number. A tile qualifying for Reserve goes directly there and you draw again. Buying one tile from a two-tile stack leaves its space occupied, so there is no refill.
answers.evidence: Refill rules specify sliding, rightmost replacement, duplicate stacking and redrawing, sorting only new tiles, and Reserve-eligible draws going straight to Reserve. A one-tile purchase from a duplicate stack causes no refill.

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles to Reserve except Largest Wine Cellar. From then on, newly drawn Service tiles also go directly to Reserve, with the same exception. After courtship 2, move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve; later PR1 draws go directly there. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. A full Market refresh is standard after each of the first three courtships, after Reserve movement.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve: Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar after courtship 1; PR1 tiles after courtship 2; later matching draws go directly to Reserve. Refresh is required after each of the first three courtships.

answers.answer: At an ordinary courtship, first return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall. For courtships 1–3, score tile VP in the current face-up theme category, including negative values; only the face-up hybrid category counts. The highest score gets one VP card and chooses one Fairchild for hand. If tied for highest, each tied player draws a VP card and no one receives a Fairchild. Every player discards one secret objective; shuffle the discards and put them on the bottom of the objective deck. After courtships 1–3, the first-player marker passes anticlockwise.
answers.evidence: Courtship and seasonal upkeep describes Fairchild return, theme scoring, award and tie rule, objective discard, and passing the first-player marker anticlockwise.

answers.answer: At final courtship, return the Fairchilds and score tile VP for all four revealed themes; a repeated category counts each time, including negative VP. Highest score gets one VP card and a Fairchild. Ties are broken by highest reputation level, ignoring wheel position; if still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied players draw VP cards under the courtship tie rule. Discard the final objective. Before scoring, players get a final chance to use special actions and VP cards for benefits where possible; then move the marker to Wedding Bells and score.
answers.evidence: Final courtship section specifies all four themes, tie handling, objective discard, last chance for special actions and VP-card benefits, then Wedding Bells and scoring.

answers.answer: End-game VP comes from improvement tiles (all face-up printed VP, including negative and unused tiles); gentry in hand and discard (including family and final Fairchild, excluding dismissed guests); fulfilled remaining objectives; reputation; servants; wealth; and retained unused VP cards. Reputation levels 1–7 score 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, and 28 VP. Wealth scores 1 VP per £200, rounded down. Game ties: a tied player with the final Fairchild wins; otherwise highest reputation level wins; if still tied, victory is shared. Wheel position does not break the tie.
answers.evidence: Final VP table lists categories and reputation values; wealth is “1 VP per £200, rounded down.” Tie rule is final Fairchild, then reputation level, then shared victory.

answers.answer: Normally each player gets five objectives at setup and two more on round 6. Each player discards one at each of four courtships, leaving three for scoring. Simultaneous discards are shuffled together and placed face down on the bottom of the deck. A tile objective requires owning the named tile(s) at game end; the tile need not be upgraded.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards states five at setup plus two on round 6, one discard at each courtship leaving three, simultaneous discards shuffled and bottom-decked, and tile objectives do not require upgrades.

answers.answer: A VP card may be used immediately when drawn, at any time on a later turn of your own (including several cards), and once more after final courtship before scoring. Reveal and discard it to use its benefit; used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained cards stay hidden with objectives and score their printed VP at game end; a card cannot provide both benefit and VP.
answers.evidence: VP card rules state use timing, used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck, retained cards stay hidden, and the player cannot take both benefit and final VP.

answers.answer: A normal activity tile must flip to its rose/upgrade side after its first use; an already-upgraded normal tile stays upgraded on later uses. A hybrid starts with its underlined category icon showing and flips after every use. A tile that upgrades into an ongoing monument (Queen’s Suite or Lionheart Suite) hosts its front activity once, upgrades into the monument, and cannot host again; its monument benefit begins on later turns. At courtship and for objectives, only a hybrid’s currently face-up category counts.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects describes mandatory first-use upgrade, hybrids flipping every use and current category counting, and suites becoming monuments that cannot host again.

answers.answer: On a hosting turn, the round-track event resolves before ongoing monument and Servants’ Hall effects; on a pass, servants and gentry are recovered first, then the event and ongoing effects resolve. Monuments give one reputation per ordinary turn during the ongoing-effects step, whether hosting or passing; there is no monument income during courtship. Servants’ Hall uses any one available servant to reduce one opponent’s reputation by one and gain one reputation yourself; that servant cannot serve the activity and is expended at turn end. It cannot target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Passing give the respective event/effect order. Improvements and ongoing effects states monument timing and Servants’ Hall servant use, effect, destination, and minimum-reputation restriction.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite uses one footman on the tile and one casual guest from hand, with that guest’s normal service; it doubles all the guest’s favours, including negative ones, then upgrades and remains an activity tile. Queen’s Suite uses a housekeeper on the tile and one prestige guest from hand, with the guest’s normal service; double one chosen favour and resolve other favours normally, then it upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite uses a butler on the tile and draws one prestige guest from the deck to attend; no personal guest service is needed. It doubles nonnegative favours, excludes negative favours from doubling, keeps the guest and puts it in discard at cleanup, then upgrades into a monument. Each suite has a fixed count of one guest; no effect can increase or decrease it.
answers.evidence: Suite activity table lists each tile’s service and guest source, service, doubling, and later state. It states all three have a fixed count of one guest that no effect may change.
